page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-90 is a high-density, compute-focused virtual machine instance built on dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 90 vCPUs across 45 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 177 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of approximately 1.97 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache sizing includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 support, as well as hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic operations. The instance does not feature local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier parallel compute throughput across diverse execution workloads. In stress-ng, the machine registers 129,122.14 points in multi-core execution, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 87,356.80 and extended instruction score of 113,336.73. Single-core performance sits in the middle-to-upper brackets, marked by a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 1,879 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2,863.38. Software compilation tests via Clang reach 63,525.00 points, while ray tracing benchmarks score 94,867.00 points, confirming dense multi-threaded efficiency.

The memory subsystem exhibits strong uncached read bandwidth at 215.31 GB/sec, while write bandwidth stabilizes at 78.98 GB/sec. This memory architecture supports heavy I/O operations, demonstrated by 116.26 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and static web throughput of 51.24 GB/sec. Quantitative LLM inference benchmarks reveal adequate prompt processing throughput for small (3,803 tokens/sec) and medium (214 tokens/sec) language models, though generation throughput scales moderately due to the absence of specialized tensor or GPU acceleration.

Operating with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 2:1, c3d-highcpu-90 maximizes compute capability per dollar without bearing the cost overhead of unneeded memory reserves. The machine is best suited for compute-bound batch processing, large-scale CI/CD software compilation pipelines, distributed web serving layers, video rendering, and multi-threaded analytical simulation workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-90 is a compute-focused instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 90 dedicated vCPUs spanning 45 physical cores alongside 177 GB of system RAM, yielding a lean 1.97 GB per vCPU ratio. Integrated instructions include AVX-512 with VNNI, bfloat16, and hardware cryptography extensions. The instance omits local NVMe disks and discrete GPUs, routing storage over network volumes. Synthetic benchmarks illustrate upper-tier multi-threaded capacity, attaining 129,122.14 in multi-core stress-ng tests, 87,356.80 in PassMark CPU tests, and 63,525.00 in Clang compilation. Memory throughput remains robust with 215.31 GB/sec uncached reads and 116.26 million Redis SET operations per second. This hardware profile provides high CPU density and cost efficiency for compute-intensive workloads such as distributed CI/CD builds, ray tracing, web serving clusters, and batch data processing.
